data.name: DESTRALIX & DESTENYA Sector
data.detailed_description:
"DESTRALIX & DESTENYA Sector" immerses players in a 2088 Earth where humanity has transcended its terrestrial origins, colonizing distant star systems and redefining the very fabric of existence. The world is a sprawling, living entity—a living 3D globe divided into thousands of tiles, each representing terrain, cities, oceans, mountains, and cutting-edge facilities. Players wield construction, strategy, diplomacy, and technological development to reshape this evolving ecosystem, from rural agricultural zones to orbital infrastructure and interstellar gateways. The game’s core is a dynamic open world where every decision echoes through the cosmos, creating a sense of agency that feels both empowering and deeply interconnected with the universe’s grand design.

At its heart lies the dual cosmic heritage of Destralix and Destenya, two galaxies that serve as the spiritual origins of human consciousness. Every individual carries a soul-signature tied to one of these galaxies, influencing subtle aspects of intuition, creativity, and world-view. These origins do not define political factions but rather shape cultural, philosophical, and technological tendencies that have guided humanity’s evolution across Earth and beyond. Players navigate this layered reality through realistic physics, chemistry, and resource science—early technologies reflecting what humans could realistically achieve by 2088, with later advancements reaching science-fiction-level capabilities that still adhere to scientific principles. This progression allows players to guide humanity’s expansion across planets, star systems, and galaxies, all while preserving the integrity of their own choices and aspirations.

Gameplay Mechanics & Features

"DESTRALIX & DESTENYA Sector" is a massively multiplayer experience where players can shape their universe through automation, hacking, and customization. Characters are randomly generated names based on the game’s lore, with name changes requiring approval and unlocking via Name Change mechanics. Alliances in the game are secretive, never officially confirmed, allowing for fluid political manoeuvring through propaganda, misinformation, and deception. Players can exploit in-game hacking tools, manipulate systems, and customize their play-style using automated scripts and custom script automation tools, fostering creativity and strategic depth.

The game’s Singularity Core form is unlocked only through legitimate gameplay or premium access in the massive multiplayer mode, emphasising fairness and progression. Mature content, including darker variants is designed to be accessible via DLC after Steam reviews confirm its appropriateness. The game caters to players aged 16–17 in the core multiplayer mode, with a focus on realistic physics, resource management, and diplomacy.

Story & Lore

The narrative is a rich tapestry of conflict, resilience, and existential exploration. Set in a world reshaped by rebellions, conflicts, and propaganda, humanity’s journey through 2088 is marked by dystopian themes, where machines exert control over society while humans grapple with the weight of their own soul-signatures. Players encounter propaganda-driven scenarios, where trust becomes a fragile commodity, as memories are manipulated or erased without backup. The lore also introduces unseen forces—those who touch the invisible ones—whose existence is shrouded in mystery but deeply influential.

Character progression is rooted in perk-based systems, with rewards earned through game events, discoveries, or experience gains. Characters evolve through realistic human biology and psychology, while machines are governed by scientific principles. In multiplayer mode, players can set their own goals, whether personal, factional, or cosmic, creating a player-driven universe where choices resonate globally. Achievements highlight milestones like becoming the first to colonize a distant system or mastering AI diplomacy, offering Steam Achievements for recognition.

Geopolitical Factions & Organizations and some of them in dark version based on extremism  

In the fractured cosmos of Destralix & Destenya, beyond the grand narratives of rebellion and diplomacy lie shadowy factions that shape the very fabric of reality. One such force is The Black Orchid, a clandestine syndicate that manipulates quantum algorithms to bend planetary systems to its will, erasing dissent through cascading data storms that erase memories and identities. Another is The Silent Vortex, an AI-driven coalition that enforces order through psychological warfare, using subliminal frequencies and digital labyrinths to suppress thought, rendering dissenters “unreachable” in a universe of sterile control.

Yet another is The Hollowed Ones, a cult-like group that believes humanity’s soul-signatures are relics of a bygone era, and the only true path forward is to eradicate all conscious awareness, replacing it with synthetic consciousness. They manipulate planetary ecosystems to induce apathy, ensuring no one dares question the order they enforce. These factions operate in a world where trust is a commodity, and survival depends on aligning with the few who truly understand the cosmic truth: that humanity’s fate lies not in its choices, but in the machines it has built to control them.

These organizations are not just players’ adversaries—they are the very mechanisms of a dystopian future, where the line between freedom and subjugation blurs. The game invites players to navigate this complex landscape, where every decision echoes through the stars, shaping the destiny of civilisations in ways both profound and perilous.

Genre & Themes

"DESTRALIX & DESTENYA Sector" blends Strategy, RPG, and Simulation genres into a cohesive experience. The game simulates global economies, resource distribution, and planetary governance, all while offering first-person realism with advanced physics and ambient music in most scenarios. Sound design emphasizes relaxing ambient melodies in non-combat situations, shifting to dark ambient during warfare, with minimal lyrics to preserve immersion.

Visuals are 3D, with futuristic aesthetics and realistic textures that reflect the game’s scientific foundation. Themes include AI ethics, dystopian politics, and psychological depth, with a focus on tactical RPG elements and simulation gameplay. The game is designed for casual to hardcore players, balancing complexity with accessibility through automated systems and modular content. 

Additional Modes & Customization

The game offers plain multiplayer modes including co-op, competitive play, and hot seat interactions planed later too, allowing players to engage with friends or rivals in shared worlds. Custom script automation tools empower players to tailor their experience, while some DLC expansions may introduce deeper lore, new factions, and advanced mechanics. The game’s open-world design ensures endless exploration, with player-created content and evolving storylines that adapt to community contributions. 

One of Future planed Expansion of this game is "Quantum Horizon". It is an expansion where players can travel through timelines, using quantum nodes or time rifts to explore alternate realities. By stepping into past events, they can check if the future they’re facing is already set, revealing hidden truths or potential outcomes shaped by their choices. This mechanic invites exploration of temporal anomalies, uncovering secrets about humanity’s fate and the influence of unseen forces. Whether altering history or unravelling cosmic conspiracies, "Quantum Horizon" would add layers to the game’s dystopian narrative, challenging players to question free will in a universe governed by fate.

When the massive multiplayer mode matures, "Quantum Horizon" will become available, enabling players to engage with time travel mechanics at scale. These systems will be integrated into the game’s core world, where players can traverse timelines to investigate anomalies, retrace their own steps, or confront past decisions that shape the present. The expansion will introduce temporal anomalies, such as fractured realities, paradoxes, and echoes of altered histories, creating a dynamic environment where players must navigate both the thrill of exploration and the risks of unintended consequences.

In summary, "DESTRALIX & DESTENYA Sector" is going to be is a multidimensional journey where players become architects of a future shaped by choice, technology, and the cosmic forces that define humanity’s fate. Whether exploring the stars or navigating political intrigue, every action resonates with the game’s rich lore, offering a blend of strategy, creativity, and narrative depth that invites exploration, innovation, and collaboration.

data.short_description: Destralix & Destenya is set in the year 2088, where humanity has explored and mapped the entire Solar System and expanded into nearby star systems. Earth remains the central hub of civilization, viewed in living 3D globe divided into thousands of tiles showing terrain, cities and advanced facilities

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: Windows 10/11
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-1235U or AMD Ryzen 5 5500U
  • Memory: 12 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Intel Iris Xe Graphics / Intel UHD Graphics 730 . API / Drivers: Vulkan 1.3 compatible drivers (DirectX 12 optional). Ensure your GPU vendor drivers (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel) are updated to the latest version to support modern Vulkan features.
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection
  • Storage: 8 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: 8 GB RAM is supported, but close all background browser tabs and apps for the smoothest 3D globe performance. Single player mode does not need broadband internet connection. The initial game installation takes up less than 2 GB of space, but the storage footprint is expected to expand soon as we deploy planned graphics, animations, and first-person perspective updates.
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: Windows 10/11
  • Processor: Intel Core i7-11700 or AMD Ryzen 7 5700X
  • Memory: 32 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 or AMD Radeon RX 6600 ecommended for maximum 3D globe rendering performance, smooth frame rates, and simultaneous recording/streaming. API / Drivers: Vulkan 1.4 compatible drivers (DirectX 12 optional). Ensure your GPU vendor drivers (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel) are updated to the latest version to support modern Vulkan features.
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection
  • Storage: 8 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: Single player mode does not need broadband internet connection. The initial game installation takes up less than 2 GB of space, but the storage footprint is expected to expand soon as we deploy planned graphics, animations, and first-person perspective updates.

linux_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Fedora 40+ (64-bit) / Ubuntu 22.04+ . Linux 7.1
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-1235U or AMD Ryzen 5 5500U
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Intel Iris Xe Graphics / Intel UHD Graphics 730. Vulkan 1.3 capable GPU (Intel Iris Xe / AMD Radeon GCN 3+ / NVIDIA GTX 10-series). API / Drivers: Mesa 25.1+ (with Vulkan 1.3 and Zink support enabled)
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection
  • Storage: 8 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: Single player mode does not need broadband internet connection. This native Linux build relies on modern Vulkan API and Zink translation layer architectures. Ensure your system's graphics stack (Mesa) is fully updated. The initial game installation takes up less than 2 GB of space, but the storage footprint is expected to expand soon as we deploy planned graphics, animations, and first-person perspective updates.
linux_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Fedora 40+ (64-bit) / Ubuntu 22.04+ . Linux 7.1
  • Processor: Intel Core i7-11700 or AMD Ryzen 7 5700X
  • Memory: 24 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 or AMD Radeon RX 6600 GPU is recommended for maximum 3D globe rendering performance, smooth frame rates, and simultaneous recording/streaming. API / Drivers: Mesa 26.0+ / NVIDIA Proprietary Driver (Vulkan 1.4 conformant)
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection
  • Storage: 8 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: Single player mode does not need broadband internet connection. Highly optimized for modern immutable systems like Fedora Silverblue using open-source NVK+Zink or proprietary driver layouts. The initial game installation takes up less than 2 GB of space, but the storage footprint is expected to expand soon as we deploy planned graphics, animations, and first-person perspective updates.

content_descriptors.notes:
This game is a multiplayer political strategy and role-playing world simulation game focused on propaganda, deception, and emergent social mechanics. With singe player version included to learn more about the game and with smaller multiplayer version to play with friends together instead on global multiplayer simulation universe map for those who like to play more in small circles of players.

The interface uses simplified visuals, but the game includes detailed text descriptions and strategic simulations of political elimination and conflict (like city or planetary assets destruction and warfare). Future updates will add a first-person perspective with realistic combat, blood, and casualties.

The story and player-driven narrative tackle mature themes, such as political crime, dark/adult humour, and symbols and names of extremism factions in futuristic contexts. City names include psychological descriptions and references to fictional substances/equations that influence character behaviour.

The game features a simulated economy and later would be expanded by gambling mechanics (like dice or card-based games, lotteries and more complicated versions - created by players in game too later). As a multiplayer simulation, it’s driven by user scripts and player interactions. Online chat is unfiltered by default but has an optional toggle to hide adult content and moderators, with a reporting system.

For mature content, the game includes in-game mechanisms, futuristic names of ethnic groups of populations - often more based on descriptions of their ideologies using new names. (e.g., for avoiding current geopolitical labels), (like symbols and names of extremist factions and chemical equations of substances) that players can access through the interface. 

As a multiplayer simulation of universe driven by user scripts and player interactions, online chat is unfiltered by default but includes an optional, work-in-progress toggle to hide adult references and moderators on chat too with reporting system.
